items.title: The philosophy of liberalism and how it has transformed our institutions
items.description:
Jonathan Rauch, author and senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, dives into the philosophy of liberalism, how it has created and transformed our institutions, and the state of truth in a world rife with misinformation.  
 This video  The philosophy of liberalism and how it has transformed our institutions  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: What genome editing tech has done for the world, so far
items.description:
Fourteen years after co-inventing CRISPR, Jennifer Doudna checks in on what it’s become. The Nobel Prize-winning biochemist walks through the technology’s biggest moments — the 2012 discovery, the 2018 CRISPR babies announcement, and today’s $2 million but functionally curative therapy for sickle cell disease — alongside newer applications like reducing methane emissions from cattle farming.

items.title: 25 years later, “Donnie Darko” is finally getting a sequel
items.description:
By all accounts,  Donnie Darko  shouldn’t exist.  
 The film, which turns 25 years old this year, ran into numerous obstacles both before and during its storied production. items.title: The Higgs boson’s most important puzzle remains unsolved
items.description: In some ways, the deepest question one can ask about our physical reality is simply, “What is the Universe made of?” In the early 1800s, we thought we knew the answer: atoms. items.title: Most accurate cosmic clocks show unexpected instability
items.description:
In all the cosmos, pulsars are the most precise long-term way to measure time. 
 
 
 
 The rate of orbital decay of a binary pulsar is highly dependent on the speed of gravity and the orbital parameters of the binary system. We have used binary pulsar data to constrain the speed of gravity to be equal to the speed of light to a precision of 99.8%, and to infer the existence of gravitational waves decades before LIGO and Virgo detected them. items.title: “Donnie Darko” offers a time travel lesson you won’t find elsewhere
items.description: In film, there are many ways to tell a story that involves time travel. Some movies, such as the  Terminator  franchise, simply include the phenomenon as a plot device, reckoning that the technical explanation is unimportant to the plot. Other times, as in  Groundhog Day , characters get stuck in a time loop, only breaking out of it once a moral lesson is learned.
